text: The deferral is the defer branch of the one published committee-decision operation, POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision (API-S7-002) on /api/recovery/writeoff/v1 with right A, taking a CommitteeDecision and answering a DecisionLogEntry; the operation, the element names, the right and the six error codes are copied from TSD S7 T-A.1 and T-A.2, the element properties from API Specification v4, each error condition is bound to one message of the legacy set, and no second path is declared.
why: TSD S7 T-A.1 publishes the operation with the request CommitteeDecision, the answer DecisionLogEntry and the right A, and T-A.2 gives the error status codes with no message ID per condition, while TSD S7 T3.1 gives no property of either element and API Specification v4 does. Declaring a second operation for a defer, or leaving the element names to the builder, would invent an interface the sources do not have.

text: The review date is declared as an optional additive property reviewDate of format date on the CommitteeDecision element, is validated as present on a defer under R-WO-18, and is recorded in the decision record and carried in the case-move answer; it has no field ID, no column in write_off and no list of values in any source, and a review date in the past is neither validated nor messaged because no source publishes a rule for it.
why: R-WO-17 and R-WO-18 turn on review_date, yet the published CommitteeDecision carries only decision, resolutionReference and membersPresent, the FSD field catalog of A2.8.3.2 names no review-date field, TSD S7 T3.1 lists no such column and TSD S7 T3.2 publishes no list. Inventing a column, a field ID, a range or a past-date rule would be a business value; the additive optional property is the smallest change that lets the rule be tested.
read: API Specification v4, CommitteeDecision; FSD S7 A2.8.3.1 and A2.8.3.2; TSD S7 T3.1 and T3.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-17 and R-WO-18; legacy RWB-E6-020 AC1, AC2 and Data

text: The published CommitteeDecision element of API Specification v4 is the baseline of the request, with its decision enumeration approve, reject and defer, its resolutionReference and its membersPresent, and the reject story's reason and this story's review date are declared as additions rather than as properties the specification publishes; the defer member is named as this story's branch and the other two as other stories'.
why: TSD S7 T-A.2 gives only the element name, so the properties must come from the second source that has them, and API Specification v4 publishes the element with three properties and a three-member decision set. Copying them character for character keeps the shared operation consistent and makes the additions visible instead of hidden.

text: The review timer of R-WO-17 is a durable timer inside WriteOffWorkflow on task queue rwb-writeoff in namespace rwb-recovery, fired once for R-WO-19 and cancelled when the case leaves DEFERRED; the timer row of DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 is created and cancelled by rwb-case on this service's answer, at an operation name that carries the placeholder, and no Temporal Schedule is declared because a review date is not a recurrence.
why: S7 owns one table only (context pack), so no timer table is its own, and the legacy timer entity with task_id and expires_at is rwb-case's in the target. JOB-05 implements TimerScheduler for every caller and is not S7's job row, while DP-10 is absent from this key's pattern set, so a Schedule or a kit registration would be a dependency the plan does not hold. A durable workflow timer needs neither a table nor a Schedule.
